newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. Fed's Greenspan to meet China's Jiang Zemin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed's Greenspan to meet China's Jiang Zemin.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan was scheduled to meet China's President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin in Beijing on Thursday, Chinese officials said.

Greenspan, visiting China at the invitation of the central bank, was due to also meet Chen Jinhua, chairman of the State Planning Commission, and Finance Minister Liu Zhongli before leaving early on Friday for Tokyo, officials of China's central bank said.
The central bank, Greenspan's host for his second visit to China, declined to say what the two sides would discuss.

Central bank officials have said Greenspan's visit was part of normal exchanges with the Federal Reserve, which has had a cooperative relationship with China's central bank for more than a decade, offering technical exchanges and training.
China has been trying to give its central bank greater autonomy and diplomats say it is eager to study the methods of other central banks around the world.
On Wednesday, Greenspan met China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji and central bank governor Dai Xianglong.

Zhu told Greenspan he hoped for greater cooperation between their two central banks and outlined details of China's financial reforms as well its reforms of lumbering state enterprises, local media said.
On his arrival, Greenspan said he was looking forward to his two days of talks in Beijing but declined further comment.
It was Greenspan's second visit to China.
